chunks: From him, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
When you recite the Adhan and the Iqamah, two rows of angels pray behind you, and when you recite the Iqamah, one row of the angels pray behind you.

key_terms.أَذَّنْتَ: You recite the Adhan (call to prayer)
key_terms.أَقَمْتَ: You recite the Iqamah (call to establish prayer)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward of angels praying behind the person reciting the Adhan and Iqamah?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to emphasize the celestial validation of the muezzin's role, where the presence of angels praying behind him signifies divine approval and spiritual elevation. This tradition underscores the unique status of the Adhan and Iqamah as acts of worship that bridge the earthly congregation with the heavenly realm, a concept deeply rooted in Shia hadith literature regarding the merits of prayer rituals.
